## Custom themes and color palettes

The chapters use stock `ggplot2` themes and plain hex codes so the code
runs in your project with nothing extra to install. This book's own
figures are styled with a small set of CT DPH brand helpers, kept in
`preamble-themes.R` at the root of the book's repository.

If you work at DPH — or you just want to see how a house style gets
packaged up — this section is the reference. These aren't part of
`ggplot2`; you'd `source()` the file into your own project to use them.

### Theme functions

| Function | What it does | Use when… |
|---|---|---|
| `theme_ct_vertical()` | Removes the y-axis line, y-axis tick marks and x-axis tick marks. Sets axis titles in bold. | Vertical / tall plots (time series, vertical bars) |
| `theme_ct_horizontal()` | Removes the x-axis line, x-axis tick marks and y-axis tick marks. Sets axis titles in bold. | Horizontal / wide plots (horizontal bars, side-by-side comparisons) |
| `theme_poppins_bold_all()` | Sets every bit of text in the plot in bold face. | When you want a uniform, no-nonsense look across all elements |

Theme functions stack — call them with `+` like any other ggplot2 layer.
Later themes fill gaps left by earlier ones, so the ordering matters
only when they overlap.

### Color palettes

| Object | Colors returned |
|---|---|
| `list_ct_primary_colors` | `primary` (#3371E7), `primary_shade1` (#00214D), `primary_shade2` (#003D9C), `primary_shade3` (#7094F5), `primary_shade4` (#C6D4FB) |
| `list_ct_secondary_colors` | `secondary` (#F27124), `secondary_shade` (#FAAA19) |
| `list_ct_tertiary_colors` | `tertiary` (#D8343E), `tertiary_shade` (#94343E) |
| `list_old_sha_colors` | Legacy SHA palette — use only for backward-compat with older reports |
| `list_color_hex_codes` | Nested list of all palettes above (flat list of named hex values) |

**Prefer the named variables over hex literals.** If the brand updates
its palette, a single change to `preamble-themes.R` propagates to every
plot that sources it.

To pick one or two named colors inside a scale, slice the list and
`unlist()` it so the scale gets a plain character vector:

```{r}
#| label: palette-example
library(ggplot2)
source(file.path(here::here(), "preamble-themes.R"))

ggplot() +
  geom_col(aes(x = factor(c("Confirmed", "Probable")), y = c(15, 25),
               fill = factor(c("Confirmed", "Probable")))) +
  labs(x = "Case status", y = "New cases", fill = "Case status") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = unlist(
      list_ct_primary_colors[c("primary_shade1", "primary_shade3")],
      use.names = FALSE
    )
  ) +
  theme_poppins_bold_all() +
  theme_ct_vertical()
```

## Interactive Maps

::: {.callout-tip}
## Want to go further with `leaflet`?

The data visualization chapter gets you comfortable with `mapview` for
quick looks and `leaflet` basics like `addTiles()`, `addPolygons()`,
`addMarkers()`, and `colorBin()` for choropleths. There's more under
the hood once you're ready for it — layer controls with `addLayers()`,
juggling coordinate and data bindings, and wiring maps up to Shiny for
interactivity. A deeper dive into all of that is coming soon.
:::
